questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require follow-up before starting infliximab.

rationale.correct: Latent TB, a draining fistula, B12 deficiency and smoking all need action before or with biologic therapy.

perOption.r1: Latent TB can reactivate on anti-TNF therapy; it must be treated first.
perOption.r4: A fistula; an abscess must be drained before anti-TNF therapy.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues before biologic therapy in Crohn disease.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is more typical of Crohn disease or ulcerative colitis.

rows.text: Disease in the terminal ileum with skip areas
Fistulas
Continuous inflammation starting at the rectum
Bloody diarrhea as the main symptom
B12 deficiency
Smoking worsens the disease

rationale.correct: Crohn disease is patchy and full thickness, often in the ileum, with fistulas and B12 deficiency.

perOption.r1:c1: Crohn disease can affect any part of the gut, in patches.
perOption.r1:c2: Crohn disease can affect any part of the gut, in patches.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze Crohn disease against ulcerative colitis.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Before the first infliximab dose, the priority is to {{b1}}. Starting it without this could cause {{b2}}.

rationale.correct: A positive TB screen must be treated before anti-TNF therapy.

perOption.b1:a: Usually at least 1 month of latent TB treatment first.
perOption.b1:b: Live vaccines are avoided on anti-TNF therapy.
perOption.b2:a: TNF blockade weakens the granulomas that contain TB.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Which parts of the infusion plan should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Premedication as prescribed, such as acetaminophen and an antihistamine
Vital signs before and during the infusion
Give the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine on the same day
Infuse rapidly over 15 minutes to save chair time

rationale.correct: Premedicate, monitor, have emergency drugs ready, correct B12, and avoid live vaccines.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Isoniazid with pyridoxine for 1 month, then infliximab 5 mg/kg. Smoking cessation. B12 injections. Colorectal surgery to examine the fistula.

questions.stem: Thirty minutes into the second infusion, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the IV line open with 0.9% sodium chloride
Give the remaining dose by IV push

rationale.correct: An infusion reaction with wheezing and low pressure means stopping, keeping access and treating.

questions.stem: At the 3-month visit, for each statement or finding, indicate whether it shows the plan is working or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Two formed stools a day; weight up 3 kg
CRP 6 mg/L
"I'll call if I get a fever or a cough that won't go away."
"I'm still smoking a pack a day."
"I got the nasal flu vaccine at the pharmacy."
Fistula drainage has stopped

perOption.r3:c1: Infection warning signs on a biologic.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require follow-up.

rationale.correct: High ileostomy output with kidney injury, electrolyte losses and orthostasis.

perOption.r1: High output (above about 1,500 mL a day) risks dehydration.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of a high-output ileostomy.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client's dehydration is made worse by {{b1}}, because {{b2}}.

options.text: drinking large amounts of plain water
water without salt pulls sodium into the bowel and is lost through the stoma
water is fully absorbed in the small bowel
sports drinks contain too much sodium
the colon is absorbing the water

rationale.correct: Without a colon, plain water increases ileostomy losses; oral rehydration solution is needed.

perOption.b1:a: Hypotonic fluid draws sodium into the gut and increases output.
perOption.b2:a: An oral rehydration solution with enough sodium is absorbed better.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each problem, indicate its priority.

rows.text: Dehydration with acute kidney injury
Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia
Falls from orthostatic hypotension
Body image concerns about the stoma

rationale.correct: Fluid, electrolytes and falls come first; body image is addressed soon after.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize problems with a high-output ileostomy.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: An oral rehydration solution instead of plain water
Thickening foods such as bananas, rice, applesauce and pasta
Encourage more plain water and sugary drinks
A high-fiber diet with raw vegetables right away

rationale.correct: Replace losses, use oral rehydration solution and thickening foods, and slow transit.

perOption.f: Raises output and blockage risk early on.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.educationalObjective: Generate solutions for a high-output ileostomy.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: IV 0.9% sodium chloride with KCl. Magnesium sulfate IV. Oral rehydration solution. Loperamide before meals. Wound, ostomy and continence nurse consult.

questions.stem: The client is ready to learn pouch care. Which teaching should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Empty the pouch when it is one-third to one-half full
Cut the barrier opening 1/8 inch (3 mm) larger than the stoma
Report a stoma that turns dark red, purple or black
Expect formed stools from the stoma once it has fully healed
Irrigate the ileostomy each morning to regulate the output

rationale.correct: Empty early, fit the barrier closely, watch stoma color and review medicines.

perOption.e: Ileostomy output stays liquid to pasty.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

rows.label: Skin
cells: Red, weepy skin around the stoma

questions.stem: Before discharge, for each finding, indicate whether it shows readiness or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Output 900 to 1,100 mL a day, pasty
Changes the pouch independently with a good seal
Skin around the stoma red and weepy
"I'll drink oral rehydration solution if output goes up or it's hot."
"I'm not going back to the gym, everyone will know."
Home supplies and ostomy nurse follow-up arranged

rationale.correct: Self-care and fluid plans are in place; skin problems and body image need follow-up through the team.

perOption.r3:c1: Barrier opening or leak needs review by the ostomy nurse.
perOption.r3:c2: Barrier opening or leak needs review by the ostomy nurse.
perOption.r5:c1: Body image concern; offer support and an ostomy support group.
perOption.r5:c2: Body image concern; offer support and an ostomy support group.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate action.

rationale.correct: Pain, fever and jaundice (Charcot triad) with hypotension point to cholangitis with sepsis.

perOption.s8: A risk factor, not an acute sign.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate what it reflects.

rows.text: Bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 420 units/L
Dark urine and pale stools
Temperature 39.4 C and WBC 19,400
Blood pressure 94/56 mm Hg
Lipase 38 units/L

rationale.correct: A stone blocking the common bile duct has caused infection and sepsis.

perOption.r3:c1: Conjugated bilirubin goes to the urine, not the stool.
perOption.r3:c2: Conjugated bilirubin goes to the urine, not the stool.
perOption.r3:c3: Conjugated bilirubin goes to the urine, not the stool.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client needs {{b1}}, and the INR of 2.8 matters because {{b2}}.

options.text: antibiotics, fluids and urgent drainage of the bile duct
ERCP with sphincterotomy carries a bleeding risk
it is in the normal range

rationale.correct: Cholangitis with sepsis needs antibiotics, fluids and ERCP drainage, with anticoagulation managed first.

perOption.b2:a: Warfarin may need reversal before the procedure.
perOption.b2:c: It is therapeutic but raises procedural bleeding risk.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which preparations for ERCP should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hold warfarin and give vitamin K as prescribed
Give a fatty meal to stimulate the gallbladder

rationale.correct: Cultures, antibiotics, anticoagulation reversal, NPO and consent before ERCP.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: ERCP in the morning or sooner if unstable. Fluid bolus 30 mL/kg.

questions.stem: Four hours after ERCP with stone removal, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Check vital signs and continue IV fluids
Resume a regular diet as planned

rationale.correct: New epigastric pain to the back with a high lipase after ERCP is post-ERCP pancreatitis.

perOption.a: New severe pain radiating to the back after ERCP suggests pancreatitis.
perOption.f: Needs a plan after sphincterotomy and possible bleeding.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Review the findings 48 hours later. For each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Afebrile; blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg
Bilirubin 1.6 mg/dL
Lipase 220 units/L, pain 2 of 10
Tolerating clear liquids
Black, tarry stool and hemoglobin down 2 g/dL
No plan yet for gallbladder removal

perOption.r6:c2: Cholecystectomy is advised to prevent recurrence.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of acute hepatitis B.

questions.stem: For each marker, indicate what it means.

rows.text: HBsAg positive
IgM anti-HBc positive
Anti-HBs positive (in someone else)
HBsAg positive for longer than 6 months (in someone else)

rationale.correct: HBsAg means current infection, IgM anti-HBc means acute, anti-HBs means immunity.

content.template: The nurse should watch most closely for {{b1}}, shown by {{b2}}.

rationale.correct: Watch for liver failure: INR, mental status and glucose.

perOption.b1:a: A small share of acute hepatitis B becomes fulminant.

questions.stem: For each person exposed, select the actions the plan should include.

groups.label: The nurse with the needlestick (vaccinated, immune status unknown)

options.text: Wash the site with soap and water at once
Test anti-HBs and give HBIG and a vaccine dose if not immune
Squeeze and soak the wound in bleach
No action because infants are not at risk
Test, and vaccinate if not immune
Use barrier protection until immunity is confirmed

rationale.correct: Exposed people need testing, vaccination and, for some, immune globulin; the needlestick needs immediate reporting.

perOption.f: Infants are at high risk of chronic infection.

questions.educationalObjective: Generate an exposure plan for hepatitis B.

exhibits.title: Exposure report
exhibits.body: The nurse completed the hepatitis B series years ago; titer never checked.

questions.stem: The client's employer calls the unit asking whether the client has hepatitis. The partner asks the nurse what the diagnosis is. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the employer that no information can be shared without the client's permission
Ask the client whether the partner may be told the diagnosis
Encourage the client to tell the partner, who needs testing
Let the public health department handle required reporting
Tell the partner the diagnosis because they live together
Confirm the diagnosis to the employer to protect coworkers

rationale.correct: Share health information only with consent; required public health reporting goes through official channels.

perOption.b: The client decides who is told.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

exhibits.title: Day 2
exhibits.body: ALT 1,520 units/L; INR 1.3. The client is resting.

questions.stem: Before discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I won't share razors or toothbrushes."
"I'll avoid alcohol and ask before taking acetaminophen."
"I'll come back in 6 months to check whether the virus has cleared."
"Hepatitis B spreads by sharing a cup."
"I can donate blood once I feel better."
"My baby has had the vaccine and immune globulin."

rationale.correct: Teaching covers blood exposure, liver protection, follow-up testing and correct transmission facts.

perOption.r4:c1: Not spread by casual contact or food.
perOption.r4:c2: Not spread by casual contact or food.
perOption.r5:c1: People with hepatitis B infection cannot donate blood.
perOption.r5:c2: People with hepatitis B infection cannot donate blood.

exhibits.title: Discharge
exhibits.body: ALT falling, INR 1.1. Infant given HBIG and vaccine.

exhibits.title: GI clinic and infusion center
exhibits.body: A 29-year-old client with Crohn disease of the terminal ileum has had 6 loose stools a day, cramping in the right lower abdomen and a 5 kg weight loss over a month. The client has a draining opening near the anus. The client smokes. The gastroenterologist plans infliximab infusions.

exhibits.title: Surgical unit, postoperative day 4
exhibits.body: A 34-year-old client had a total colectomy with an end ileostomy for severe ulcerative colitis. The client is eating a regular diet and drinking plenty of water and sports drinks. The client feels dizzy when standing. The stoma is pink and moist.

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 2200
exhibits.body: A 68-year-old client with known gallstones has had right upper abdominal pain for 2 days, now with shaking chills. The client's eyes are yellow and the urine is dark like tea; stools are pale. The client takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

exhibits.title: Medical unit
exhibits.body: A 31-year-old client has had fatigue, nausea, right upper abdominal ache and dark urine for a week, and now yellow skin. The client shares a home with a partner and a 6-month-old infant. During admission, a nurse sustained a needlestick from a used needle after drawing the client's blood.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
